claims.claim: The Walking Liberty half dollar designed by Adolph A. Weinman was produced from 1916 through 1947; Benjamin Franklin replaced Liberty in 1948.

In this Walking Liberty design, Liberty strides toward the sunrise, wrapped in the flag, with her right arm extended and branches in her left; the reverse shows an eagle on a rock beside a pine branch.
claims.visualLimit: The supplied half-dollar image is an obverse photo; the reverse description is sourced history, not an assertion about the reverse of this specimen.

claims.claim: The Mint launched the American Eagle program in 1986 and used Weinman's 1916 Walking Liberty half dollar design on the Silver Eagle obverse.
The Mint refreshed the Silver Eagle reverse design in 2021 while retaining Walking Liberty on the obverse.
claims.visualLimit: The supplied Silver Eagle photo shows the obverse only; the reverse change is explained with text, not shown as a coin image.

claims.claim: The photographed Silver Eagle example is dated 2021.
claims.basis: Visible numerals on the coin in the reviewed full original and crop. No mint mark or holder grade is used.
